clue.text: Where one might take an outside gamble on getting a pail, perhaps

definitions.text: Where one might take an outside gamble on getting a pail, perhaps

parts.words: Where one might take an outside gamble on getting a pail, perhaps
parts.note: an unregistered broker's office where bets are placed on share prices outside the exchange, read also as a store selling pails

explanation.surface: A gambler wonders where to place an unofficial bet, or whether to go buy a pail.
explanation.walkthrough: A bucket shop is a back-street broker taking bets on stock prices outside the official exchange; the second reading is a shop where you might buy a pail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucket shops were unlicensed dealers taking speculative wagers on prices away from the regulated market.

clue.text: A bill the offender may have to face if caught

definitions.meaning: a bird's bill or nose-like projection

definitions.text: the offender may have to face if caught
definitions.meaning: British slang for a magistrate who hears the case

explanation.surface: A criminal who gets caught must face the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAK is old British slang for a magistrate, the official a caught offender appears before.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its beak, and slang calls a magistrate the beak.

clue.text: Shared the lead in dramatic fashion?

definitions.text: Shared the lead in dramatic fashion?

parts.words: Shared the lead in dramatic fashion?
parts.note: two actors jointly topping the bill of a play or film

explanation.surface: Someone shared the lead in a theatrical, showy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors given equal billing as principals are said to have shared star status in the production.

clue.text: More or less Important member of the cast

definitions.text: less Important member of the cast
definitions.meaning: a walk-on performer in a film or play with no lines

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an actor is more or less an important cast member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More or less' looks like one phrase; split it, with 'or' as a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional is surplus, and a background performer in a crowd scene is a film's walk-on.

clue.text: Radiant gift one might procure for a tanner?

definitions.text: Radiant gift one might procure for a tanner?

parts.words: Radiant gift one might procure for a tanner?
parts.note: a tanner is old British slang for a sixpence, but here it is someone wanting a tan, given a glowing device

explanation.surface: A shining present one might buy for sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner is old British slang for a sixpence coin, suggesting a cheap gift; here it is a person who tans, for whom an ultraviolet lamp is the ideal present.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultraviolet appliance gives skin a bronze colour indoors, so it suits someone who wants a tan.

clue.text: East German with ample funds, though quite unable to take flight

definitions.note: the definition describes the flightless bird, standing for its noun

parts.note: Ost is the German word for east
having plenty of money means rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy man from East Germany still cannot get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person from the GDR, but it asks for the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: The large African bird runs fast but has wings too small to fly.

clue.text: Whip-round for a stern old censor

parts.note: cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, is shortened to cat
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A collection is taken for a strict old official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like a collection of money; split it into a whip and a round. Cato the Elder was the Roman censor famed for his severity.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and was proverbial for austere morals.

clue.text: An unprosaic work that's positively electric

definitions.note: the definition describes the positive electrode, standing for the noun

parts.note: taken as written
a poem, not prose, such as an ode

explanation.surface: A poetic composition with an electrifying effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The positively charged electrode in a cell or valve is where current enters.

clue.text: Left sovereign behind, being a superior officer?

indicators.note: the sovereign comes behind, placed after the first part

parts.note: left behind in a race, outpaced, is outran
a monarch is a king

explanation.surface: Someone left the monarch behind while serving as a senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of higher military rank than another is to be senior to them.

clue.text: Magnificent advance amid revolutionary declines

indicators.note: amid means the advance sits inside the other piece
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for declines is read backwards

parts.note: declines, falls, means dips
to advance money is to lend

explanation.surface: A grand step forward in the middle of a revolution's decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like an adjective about the declines, but it signals reading backwards, and 'amid' places the advance in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean splendidly impressive or grand.

clue.text: Something worth having in the manner prescribed, apparently

parts.note: as means in the way that
set means laid down or prescribed

explanation.surface: A valuable thing done just as it was prescribed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As set' means in the manner prescribed, and 'apparently' is a link hinting at that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is any useful or valuable thing or quality.

clue.text: In no condition to get down to the article?

definitions.text: In no condition to get down to the article?

parts.words: In no condition to get down to the article?
parts.note: unfit for a task, and also not rising as high as the pronoun 'it', the article in question

explanation.surface: Someone is too unwell to deal with the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means unfit for a task; the second reading takes 'it' as the article one fails to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unfit for a task means lacking the strength or health to manage it.

clue.text: French husband holding a piece of capital equipment back for a glamorous female agent

indicators.note: holding means the French husband surrounds the other piece

parts.note: mari is French for husband

indicators.note: back means the words for a piece of headgear are read in reverse order

parts.note: capital means head, so headgear: a hat

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with a reversed bit of equipment, for a seductive spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means head, so its equipment is headgear; 'back' reverses it with the A, and 'holding' wraps it. Mata Hari was the Dutch dancer executed as a spy in 1917.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari, the exotic dancer shot as a German spy, became the byword for the seductive woman spy.

clue.text: An eel disconcerts her

indicators.note: disconcerts means the letters of an eel are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A slippery fish upsets a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Elena is a woman's name, so a girl could be referred to by the pronoun.

clue.text: Makes overtures to one who is paid to play among Red Indians

indicators.note: among puts the paid player inside the tribe's name

parts.note: the Apaches are a Native American people (dated term in the clue)

parts.words: one who is paid to play
parts.note: a professional, pro, is paid to play sport

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman makes advances among Native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: To make overtures is to make advances to someone, opening contact.

clue.text: Recovers spirits once fringe benefits are raised?

parts.note: perks are job extras, fringe benefits
raised means up

explanation.surface: Morale rises once job extras are increased.
explanation.definitionFit: To brighten up or regain cheerfulness is the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Stock reaction to panic

parts.note: stock means livestock, and their response to fright is a headlong rush

explanation.surface: A typical, predictable response to alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like 'standard'; it means cattle, whose panicked rush has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd of cattle running wildly in fright is the sense, extended to any frantic rush.

clue.text: Was compelled to land white fish

parts.note: had (to) means was obliged
a ship lands at a dock, so dock means land

explanation.surface: Someone was forced to land a white fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This North Atlantic cod-relative has white flesh and is popular in fish and chips.

clue.text: It leaves one on the wrong side of the bank

definitions.text: It leaves one on the wrong side of the bank

parts.words: It leaves one on the wrong side of the bank
parts.note: a river bank picture, but really a bank account in debit

explanation.surface: Something leaves a person stranded on the wrong side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowing past the balance puts an account into the red, owing the lender.

clue.text: British MPs who sportingly represent the Soviet Union?

definitions.meaning: military police, nicknamed for their red-topped caps

definitions.text: who sportingly represent the Soviet Union?
definitions.meaning: players capped for the Reds, the Soviet national side

explanation.surface: British politicians who play sport for the USSR.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs here are military police, not members of parliament; a cap is an appearance for a national team, so Soviet internationals are 'red caps'.
explanation.definitionFit: British army police wear red-topped caps, and a capped player for the Soviet Reds fits the second reading.

clue.text: Ruler's wife seen last month in the capital of Yemen?

indicators.note: in puts last month inside the capital

parts.note: Sana (Sanaa) is the capital of Yemen
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old letters

explanation.surface: A ruler's consort was seen in Yemen's capital last month.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo, old business-letter shorthand for last month) goes inside SANA. 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The consort of a Muslim ruler such as a sultan bears this title.

clue.text: Kind of winged duck? Yes

indicators.note: kind of signals a variety, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is a type of flying duck, and answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of WINGED plus O gives the answer, and 'Yes' tells you the whole clue is also its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater dabbling bird of Europe is one variety of wild duck.

clue.text: A spring and river that finishes in the Wash

definitions.text: river that finishes in the Wash

parts.note: a spring of water is a well
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spring and a river flowing into an English bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is the large bay on the east coast of England between Lincolnshire and Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welland flows through Stamford and Spalding to empty into the Wash.

clue.text: A regressive attitude for a fabulous moralist

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for an attitude is reversed

parts.note: an attitude, a stance, is a pose

explanation.surface: A backward-looking outlook suits a famous preacher of morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' reverses only the attitude, leaving the opening A in place. 'Fabulous' means telling fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek storyteller wrote fables, each ending with a moral lesson.

clue.text: 29's sound-vision?

indicators.note: sound means the word for 29 is said out loud

parts.note: the answer to clue 29, meaning situation

explanation.surface: Clue 29's sound and vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across means situation; said aloud it gives the word for vision.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of seeing is eyesight.

clue.text: Old Wycliffians backing everything in the upper chamber

indicators.note: in puts the reversed piece inside the upper chamber

parts.note: the House of Lords is the UK upper chamber

indicators.note: backing means the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: Followers of Wycliffe supporting everything in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the word for everything and 'in' puts it within the upper house of the UK parliament. Wycliffe was the 14th-century English reformer.
explanation.definitionFit: The followers of John Wycliffe, the fourteenth-century English reformer, were called by this name.

clue.text: A gipsy man with a subtly pervasive quality

parts.note: a Rom is a Romany man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Romany man with an air of quiet distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive smell or air that hangs around something, suffusing it.

clue.text: Measure of old Rome text

indicators.note: of means the answer is taken from within the following words

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman document measures something.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out or allot in portions is to apportion, as in punishment meted out.

clue.text: Exalted stage version of epic mountain climb?

definitions.meaning: an elevated, intensely exciting theatrical work
a play staged on a mountain, high up

explanation.surface: A lofty theatrical adaptation of an epic ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense theatrical excitement is the idiom, and a play performed at altitude is the literal reading.

clue.text: Give a speech or arrange tea

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of or and tea are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to either speak or prepare tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link between two definitions, but it is fodder alongside TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak formally or pompously before an audience.

clue.text: Is taken aback by the heartless situation

indicators.note: taken aback means read backwards, so is turns round
heartless means the middle letter of the word the is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised by an unfeeling position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns IS into SI; 'heartless' drops the H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or position where something is placed.

clue.text: Young seaside visitor may emerge from 11.across to build it

annotationWithheld.why: Young seaside visitor may emerge from 11.across to build it: the cross-reference gives NOT UP TO IT, which neither yields nor defines SANDCASTLE; the reference appears misnumbered or garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Young seaside visitor may emerge from 11.across to build it
